  "endpoint_class": "primary-hard",
  "concordance_definition": "The primary objective of the HESI Pro-Arrhythmia Working Group was to assess the concordance between the results of nonclinical repolarization assays and clinical QT interval prolongation.",
  "limitations_stated": [
    "Drug findings were either positive or negative as interpreted by study sponsors.",
    "Drug bath concentrations in in vitro studies were often not measured.",
    "Range of free drug exposures in nonclinical assays did not usually achieve desired 1- to 100-fold multiple of CRC.",
    "Not every drug was tested in each nonclinical assay.",
    "Bias in the dataset as sponsors typically submit drugs lacking or having limited QTc effects.",
    "Paucity of information regarding study quality.",
    "Lack of additional nonclinical and clinical information to aid data interpretation.",
    "Nonclinical studies submitted were markedly heterogeneous.",
    "Some studies were conducted prior to ICH guidelines or were not robust.",
    "The 30-fold threshold for concordance may not always be appropriate."
  ],
  "funding_conflict": "Authors employed in the pharmaceutical industry at the time of submission.",
  "key_numbers": [
    "91% of drugs that prolonged the QT interval in humans also did so in animals.",
    "88% of drugs that did not prolong the QT in humans had no effect on animals.",
    "150 drugs evaluated in the joint HESI/FDA database.",
    "31% of 150 drugs were discordant.",
    "43 thorough QT (TQT) positive drugs in the database.",
    "28 (65% of TQT positive, 19% overall) were discordant TQT-positive drugs.",
    "Sensitivity increased with higher exposure multiples for hERG and in vivo QTc assays.",
    "Specificity of all assays was consistently excellent (89-100%).",
    "Overall concordance in the database was moderate.",
    "3 drugs caused clinical QT prolongation (ΔΔQTc) ≥20 ms among discordant TQT-positive drugs.",
    "11 caused prolongation between 10 and 20 ms.",
    "14 caused prolongation < 10 ms.",
    "8 discordant TQT-negative drugs (false positives).",
    "9 of 28 discordant TQT-positive drugs had data from all 3 nonclinical assays.",
    "19 of 28 discordant TQT-positive drugs had partial nonclinical datasets.",
    "hERG assay performed best within a 30-fold multiple from the CRC.",
    "Predictivity of hERG assays is better at 45-fold clinical exposures.",
    "Drug 12 caused a mean increase of 7.7 ms in QTc with an upper 95% confidence interval > 10 ms in the TQT study.",
    "Drug 142 caused QTc prolongation at both clinical doses tested in the TQT study.",
    "Drug 173 tested positive in the TQT study, showed no effects in the hERG assay up to 60,000× the CRC.",
    "Drug 173 showed no effects in the in vivo dog telemetry study up to 12× the CRC.",
    "Women are at a greater risk for developing drug-induced QTc interval prolongation and subsequent arrhythmias.",
    "Elderly men and women tend to have longer QTc intervals than nonelderly adult men and women.",
    "20-40% of congenital long QT syndrome cases have mutations in the KCNH2 gene.",
    "QTc interval prolongation occurs repeatedly with hypothermia treatment.",
    "Terfenadine removed from the US market due to QTc prolongation and TdP risk.",
    "64% of T2DM patients showed prolonged QTc intervals."
  ]
